one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30: Q3 FY26 was reported 2026-09-10 (beat, but Q4 revenue guide midpoint $6.825B below ~$6.85B consensus; stock fell ~2-3%), Q4 FY26 earnings are expected mid-December, Adobe MAX is 2026-11-10 to 11-12 (after the window) and the CEO handover to Anil Chakravarthy is 2026-12-01. Post-earnings drift after a 'beat but soft guide' is mildly negative, while the stock sits near the lower part of its 52-week range with a ~$24.5B buyback authorization supporting it; these roughly cancel. Exogenous risk is AI-competitor launches (e.g., the Anthropic Claude Design launch knocked ADBE ~1.5% earlier this year) and peer software prints late October. So I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at today's price with monthly vol ~41%/3.5 = ~11.7%, very slightly skewed down (median ~$237).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28E non-GAAP EPS ~$30.5 x 9.5x = $290, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM FCF/share ~$27.5 at a 9.5% required yield = $289 plus ~$0 net debt; weight 0.4 but rounded with a small buyback-accretion adjustment to $295). The multiple is kept near today's depressed ~9-10x because net new ARR is falling ~37% YoY; the fair value does not assume a re-rating.

Stock trades ~9.7x FY26 and ~8.6x FY27 consensus EPS today (StreetSignal cites ~10x); consensus target $278 implies ~10x FY27. I hold roughly today's multiple (slightly above FY27-based) because ARR deceleration and AI-substitution risk (stock-photo cannibalisation, Canva/Claude Design) argue against a re-rating, but 10%+ FCF yield plus buybacks limit further compression.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 OCF $2.52B annualises to ~$10B; Q4 is seasonally strong and revenue grows ~7-8%; capex is small for Adobe, so ~$10.4B FCF in the year to Sept 2028.
391M outstanding (10-Q cover) and ~400M diluted guide; ~9.5M/quarter buyback pace partly offset by SBC -> ~378M diluted by Sept 2027.
Total debt $6.363B less cash and ST investments $5.639B.

StreetSignal notes ~10% FCF yield today; I use slightly below today's yield (market already prices a lot of disruption) but well above a typical 4-5% software FCF yield because terminal growth is in question.

bear.story: Net new ARR keeps shrinking in FY27 (freemium MAU fails to convert, stock-content and entry-level creative seats migrate to Canva, Claude Design, and model-native tools), ending-ARR growth falls to ~5-6%, new CEO resets FY27 guide lower at the December print; EPS ~$27 on a 6.5x multiple (value-trap pricing) = ~$175, with overshoot to the $160s.

base.story: ARR growth settles at ~8-9%, Q4 net new ARR bigger than Q3 as guided, AI-first ARR (>$650M, +150%) keeps compounding but does not offset core deceleration; EPS grows ~10-12% with buybacks; multiple stays ~8.5x NTM EPS of ~$30 = ~$255-260.

bull.story: Freemium funnel (>100M creative MAU, +70% YoY; >1B total MAU) converts, net new ARR re-accelerates in 2H FY27, new CEO's agentic/Acrobat/CXO story plus price increases land; market re-rates to ~11x NTM EPS of ~$31 = ~$340-350.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$175 (well under the 52-week low of $190 and ~6x forward EPS / ~15% FCF yield) the price would most likely reflect a fundamental break: FY27 guidance under the new CEO implying ending-ARR growth at or below ~5%, or evidence that AI tools are driving outright seat/ARR churn in Creative Cloud rather than just slower net adds. Ordinary volatility (41% annual) would rarely take a buyback-supported ~10x P/E stock there without that.

reasoning: Reported facts: Q3 FY26 (reported 2026-09-10) revenue $6.76B +13%, non-GAAP EPS $6.13 +15%, ending ARR $27.5B +11.2%, AI-first ARR >$650M +150%, record OCF $2.52B, FY26 guide raised to EPS $24.45-24.50, but Q4 revenue guide slightly below consensus and, per the call and independent newsletters (StreetSignal, Ampel-Update), net new ARR fell ~36-37% YoY and RPO grew only ~8%, the first single-digit print since 2023. CEO handover to Anil Chakravarthy on Dec 1. Balance sheet is near net-cash-neutral (debt $6.36B vs. cash/ST $5.64B), 391M shares, $24.55B buyback left. Lane evidence: Substack writers split between 'cheap compounder at ~10x EPS and ~10% FCF yield' (StreetSignal, Clayton-type pieces) and 'cracks/guilty until proven innocent' (Hated Moats, Pursuit of Compounding, who flagged stock-photo cannibalisation); alt-data shows huge top-of-funnel (>1B MAU, 100M+ creative freemium MAU, Adobe Express 100M+ Play downloads, 4.6 rating) but weak standalone Firefly web traffic (Semrush: 12.3M visits in June 2026, -13% m/m) and Canva leading the design category on Similarweb; job data show ~2,600 open roles and no WARN notice, i.e. quiet attrition rather than crisis; the only ADBE prediction markets were earnings-beat contracts (Polymarket ~92% beat, Sept 2026) with no bearing on the 12m view; X was not fetched. Valuation: ~$290 fair value from 9.5x FY28E EPS and a 9.5% FCF yield, i.e. ~22% above today, but I do not let the median travel there because the leading indicator (net new ARR) is deteriorating and the market has repeatedly de-rated the stock through 2026 (from ~$350 to ~$238). Base rates: 41% realized vol, typical large-cap ±25-35%. I set the 12m distribution as a lognormal with median ~$250 (EPS growth + buyback mostly offset by some multiple risk) and sigma ~0.38, with a slightly fatter left tail for the disruption/CEO-reset path and slightly thinner far-right tail; scenario mean ~$256 (bear $170 25%, base $258 50%, bull $345 25%). P(>=238) ~0.54, P(>=190) ~0.75, P(>=321) ~0.24. Research was limited to ~14 searches/fetches; sec.gov curl download failed so the 10-Q was read via web fetch.
